name: LSND
summary: LSND was a Los Alamos short-baseline experiment whose electron-antineutrino appearance excess motivated continuing searches for additional neutrino states and alternative new-physics explanations.
detection_principle: Weakly scintillating mineral oil recorded both Cherenkov and scintillation light. Inverse-beta candidates consisted of a prompt positron and a delayed 2.2 MeV gamma from neutron capture on hydrogen; timing, topology and control samples constrained backgrounds.

results.summary: Reported an electron-antineutrino excess compatible with appearance oscillations in the stated model; the signal is not a unique proof of a sterile-neutrino interpretation.

science_scope: The record describes the named experiment as one programme; detector subsystems and repeated analyses are not counted as independent experiments.
